title: Jackson M Luckey
text:
EXPERIENCE

Doctoral Researcher, Hertie School, -2025-2026

Developed machine learning models to predict residential permitting and construction times using cellphone location records, satelitte imagery, demographics, and other data.
Worked on estimating the causal effect of new housing developments on rents and house prices at the city, local, and national level.
Laid the groundwork to run an experiment on an European housing platform to measure discrimination against Roma people in housing markets and evaluate potential interventions.
Evaluated LLMs as competitive agents in simultaneous ascending auction settings.
Worked on methods for evaluating causal effects in market settings (where all units influence all other units).
Experimented with LLMs in game theory settings to try to identify triggers for undesirable strategic behavior.
Modelled the impact of changing political boundaries on support for new housing development in order to disentangle
Developed a pipeline for coding building permits (often unstructured, lots of free text) across the US to identify new housing construction permitting in cities across the US.



Teaching at Hertie School

Lab Instructor and TA for Data Structures and Algorithms, -Spring 2026
Taught the lab component of the course, developed the lab teaching materials and problem sets (as the curriculum was significantly reworked), and graded problem sets and exams.


Instructor for Python Bootcamp, -Winter 2026
Developed a curriculum and teaching materials for and then taught a 3 day (i.e. 24 hours) bootcamp introducing Python, using NumPy to implement machine learning algorithms, and then using Pandas, Polars, and Flask to work with tabular data and create APIs.


Lab Instructor and TA for Mathematics for Data Science, -Fall 2025

Taught the lab component of the course, which provides an introductory overview of probability and basic statistics, calculus, linear algebra, and optimization.
Updated labs and problem sets.
Graded problem sets and exams and helped write the exam.



Instructor for R and Math Bootcamp, -Spring 2025
Developed a curriculum and teaching materials for and then taught a 3 day (i.e. 24 hours) bootcamp on R combined with introducing statistics and linear algebra.


Lead TA for Causal Inference and Statistical Modelling, Hertie School -2024
Taught the weekly labs and graded problem sets for a course introducing causal inference and (basic) statistical modelling in R to Masters in Public Policy students.



Research Assistant for Professor Asya Magazinnik, Hertie School -2024-2026

Researched existing literature on modeling housing construction data using large indirect datasets (e.g. web searches, traffic data).
Collected known high-quality housing permitting data, converted them into a structured format using a variety of approaches (e.g. fuzzy merging, LLMs), and then built a database.
Ran simulations of conjoint surveys to determine required sample size and therefore feasibility of projects looking at political support for immigrants and changes to the built environment.
Developed a process using LLMs to fuzzy-join datasets with organization descriptions written in a variety of European languages (24 total).



Health Economist, RTI International — 2020–2023

Conducted cost-effectiveness and cost-benefit analyses of behavioral-health programs and co-authored peer-reviewed articles in health economics and policy journals.
Worked for the Health Economics team on the Healing Communities Study (a national evaluation of interventions to reduce opioid overdose deaths across four states).
Built statistical models in R, Python, and Stata to answer policy questions for stakeholders, public officials, and private-sector clients.
Developed internal packages for repeated data tasks involving EHRs and claims data.
Built data pipelines and R/Shiny dashboards so non-technical stakeholders could work with evaluation data.
Presented research and policy recommendations to academics, elected officials, health-insurance executives, and government health staff.
Mentored new staff and interns in R, Stata, and economic evaluation methods.



Data Science Education Consultant, Reed College — 2017–2020

Co-taught workshops on statistical programming (R, Python, Stata), data visualization, and spatial analysis / GIS.
Assisted students with translating thesis proposals into feasible quantitative research designs and programmed components necessary for their research. For example, creating a “lootbox” game as part of a thesis evaluating the rationality of video game players.



Statistical Analysis Intern, RTI International — Summer 2019

Modelled health outcomes for subpopulations for a post hoc analysis of a RCT.
Created visualizations of the spatial distribution of government funding for behavioral healthcare.
Designed and developed dashboards using R and Shiny for federal government clients.
Converted Stata code to Python to scale an existing statistical analysis process for use on datasets that could not be ran on a single machine.



Business Development and Intelligence Intern, FEI — Summer 2018
Developed a pipeline for combining a variety of information sources (archived emails, Excel spreadsheets, PDFs) into an organized database of funding for behavioral health interventions and potential public-private business opportunities.


Freelance Full Stack Developer — Full-time 2014–2016, intermittent part-time afterwards
Developed and updated websites using Django, Ruby on Rails, and Wordpress. Helped small businesses implement analytics to track KPIs.
